encoding.model: CU = os.environ.get("CU", None). os.environ.get(k, default) returns None iff key absent, else a str. So `CU is None` <=> env var CU is unset. Strings have no null in z3, so nullability is modeled with present:Bool (env var set?) and cu_str:String (the value when set, constrained to the seeded non-None member "64"). predicate := Not(present).
encoding.note: Pure nullability check. z3 4.16.0 exhaustively decides over the complete seeded domain {None, "64"}: both the unset case (predicate True) and the set case (predicate False) are sat. Mirrors ExpressionEvaluator unary+compare ops.

pure_helper:
from typing import Optional

def cu_is_none(cu_env: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    # Mirror of LibraryIO.getCUCount:689 guard.
    # cu_env = os.environ.get("CU", None); branch taken when cu_env is None.
    return cu_env is None

runtime_note: The predicate LOGIC is fully static (string nullability) and exhaustively solved by z3 over the complete seeded domain {None, "64"}. The value originates from os.environ.get("CU", None), an external-state read at call time. UNLIKE os.name (interpreter-set, not driveable from public input), the CU environment variable IS publicly settable: any caller/CI can export CU=<n> or leave it unset, so a caller CAN drive either branch from outside the process. Classification is solver-backed-under-assumptions: under the assumption that CU is read from os.environ (with the seeded value space), z3 decides both branches; the actual taken branch is determined by the runtime environment, not chosen by the solver. Runtime confirmed: unset -> CU=None, (CU is None)=True; CU=64 -> CU="64", (CU is None)=False. When the predicate is True the function falls through to a rocminfo subprocess probe (GPU/host dependent); the char-test CI host has no GPU, so an unset CU leads to printExit("Failed to get Compute Unit count..."). Setting CU short-circuits the probe entirely.
